title.en: Resource exclusivity, reservation order and blocked states

summary: Check that a capacity-one resource has at most one owner, that movement follows reservation, and that blocked entities are named.
objective: Ownership never exceeds capacity, movement happens only while the reservation is held, and unresolvable waits are reported as blocked.
applies_when: Entities compete for docks, machines, bays or other limited resources.
A resource can be closed, disabled or taken out of service while busy.
Approach or travel animation is tied to gaining access.
intent_signals: two trucks drove into the same dock
closing a dock while it was in use
example_prompts: Check the dock reservation rules when every dock is closed.
negative_signals: safety certification of real yard operations

principles: A capacity-one resource is a mutual-exclusion invariant: at most one owner at any model time, and ownership is acquired before the entity commits to moving.
Waiting must be observable; an entity that can never proceed under the current policy is blocked, and blocked should be a state the model can name.
Closing a busy resource needs a declared rule — rejected, deferred until release, or preempted — because all three are defensible and only one is implemented.
implementation: Record for every resource its current owner, its waiting queue and the acquisition timestamp, and evaluate ownership at each event boundary.
Run a contention fixture: more arrivals than resources, an arrival exactly at a service completion, a close request while busy, and a close of all resources while entities wait.

Compare acquisition against movement start using model time first and the queue sequence key when the two times are equal, since a reservation and the movement it authorises can legitimately commit at the same model time.
Measure waiting and service durations from model timestamps rather than animation completion callbacks, and report them with their model-time units.
observable_checks: No resource has two owners at any event boundary, and entities in service never exceed total capacity.

Every entity that starts moving toward a resource already holds the reservation at that instant: acquisition time is less than or equal to movement time, the acquisition precedes it in event-sequence order when the times are equal, and ownership is held throughout the movement. Movement without a held reservation is the failure signal.
Closing a busy resource follows exactly the declared rule with a visible outcome, and with all resources closed the waiting entities are reported as blocked rather than waiting silently forever.

known_limits: Checks the resource contract of an authored policy; it is not a scheduling optimality or utilisation study.
Authored verification guidance; no simulation was run for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.
